summary.headline: Sham Foam Ltd's ₹4,048.20 lakh SME IPO (31.14 lakh shares at ₹130) is a fixed-price issue, with FY26 PAT of ₹865.06 lakh and 9.37% PAT margin.
summary.overview: This is the prospectus document, not an earnings call, so there is no management Q&A or quarterly update. It covers a fresh issue of up to 31,14,000 equity shares at ₹130 (face value ₹10), listing on BSE SME, with issue open 11 Aug 2026 and close 13 Aug 2026. FY26 revenue from operations rose 13.77% to ₹9,231.92 lakh, EBITDA margin expanded to 11.91% from 5.78%, and PAT more than doubled to ₹865.06 lakh. Net proceeds of ₹3,500.50 lakh are earmarked for capex at the existing Ambala plant, working capital and general corporate purposes.

segments.name: PU Foam
segments.commentary: Contributed ₹7,960.10 lakh, or 86.22% of FY26 revenue from operations, down from 91.99% in FY24. Balance is mattresses and other home comfort products.

segments.name: Domestic geography
segments.commentary: Uttar Pradesh 27.34%, Punjab 21.13%, Haryana 12.98% and Delhi 11.45% of FY26 revenue. Punjab share fell from 32.27% in FY24.

guidance_outlook: Working capital requirement estimated at ₹2,756 lakh for FY27 and ₹3,359.94 lakh for FY28, to support revenue targets.
Revenue projections rely on expansion of the existing plant, pan-India dealer network and PU foam demand in furniture, garments and other industries.
Net proceeds of ₹3,500.50 lakh: ₹1,471.65 lakh capex (FY27), ₹1,425 lakh working capital (₹825 lakh FY27, ₹600 lakh FY28), ₹603.85 lakh GCP.
Post-issue installed capacity stays at 15,000 TPA; available capacity rises from 6,000 to 10,000 TPA after the expansion.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 15,000 TPA at Ambala single plant; actual production 5,257 TPA in FY26 (87.62% utilisation on cutting-machine basis), up from 78.20% in FY24.
Capex of ₹1,537.31 lakh includes civil shed ₹430.40 lakh (incl. GST) and machinery ₹1,106.91 lakh; ₹1,471.65 lakh to be funded from the issue.
Machinery quotes from A S Enterprises (30m loop slitter ₹250 lakh; long block storage ₹564 lakh; circular and vertical cutters, re-bonding machine, boiler) dated 30 July 2026; no orders placed yet.
Free space of 54,460 sq ft in the 2,04,460 sq ft facility; 10,000 sq ft earmarked for new equipment.
Capacity expansion adds 4,000 TPA of cutting capacity; no alternate funding identified.
demand_pricing: Top 10 customers 25.06% of FY26 revenue (FY24: 28.02%); top customer 2.89%. No long-term customer contracts.
Trade receivables ₹2,539.70 lakh (27.51% of revenue); receivable days 93 in FY26, projected to stay at 93 in FY27 and FY28.
Trade payable days rose to 84 in FY26 from 47 in FY24; projected 82 in FY27 and 75 in FY28.
Raw material cost ₹7,270.04 lakh (78.75% of revenue); top 10 suppliers 78.56% of purchases; no long-term supply agreements.
Competition from organised and unorganised players; Sheela Foam is a litigant (trademark 'FEATHER FRESH', claim ₹200.10 lakh, next hearing 27 Nov 2026).

qa_highlights.question: Not applicable: the document is a prospectus, not an earnings call, so no analyst questions were asked.
qa_highlights.answer: No management answers in the transcript. The closest equivalent is the prospectus disclosure on capacity: the Company says it runs at around 80% of available capacity, limited by cutting machines, with FY26 utilisation at 87.62% on a 15,000 TPA installed base.

risks_watch: Pending Sheela Foam trademark suit (claim ₹200.10 lakh) in Delhi High Court; mediation failed; next listing 27 Nov 2026.
Promoters hold 72.90% post-issue; Charming Fashion Pvt Ltd holds 32.95%. Promoter pre-IPO shares locked in for 1–3 years.
Working capital gap grows from ₹1,916.67 lakh (FY26) to ₹3,359.94 lakh (FY28); reliance on internal accruals of ₹2,407.64 lakh by FY28.
Concentration: Punjab, UP, Haryana and Delhi make up over 70% of revenue; single plant in Ambala on a related-party lease to 2055.
Multiple delayed ROC and TDS filings; no show-cause notice yet, but potential penalties.
Machinery quotes valid for 180 days; no orders placed; cost escalation risk on the ₹1,537 lakh capex.
summary.management_tone: Not applicable: this is a prospectus, not an earnings call, so there is no management commentary. The document is heavily caveated, with repeated 'no assurance' language on expansion timelines, litigation and cost estimates.
key_quotes: Currently, our Company is working at an annual capacity of around 80% of the available capacity considering the limitation of working of cutting machines and other associated machineries and equipments.

adds.what: 4,000 TPA cutting capacity expansion at Ambala plant (available capacity 6,000 to 10,000 TPA; installed 15,000 TPA unchanged)

growth.why: This is an IPO prospectus, not an earnings call: no quarterly results or explicit FY27 revenue growth % are given, only working capital sized for revenue targets (Rs 2,756 lakh FY27, Rs 3,359.94 lakh FY28) and a 4,000 TPA expansion at Ambala funded by Rs 1,471.65 lakh of IPO capex (machinery quotes dated 30 July 2026, no orders placed) with utilisation up to 87.62%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 11.91% from 5.78% in FY25 and PAT margin to 9.37% from 4.41%, but raw material is 78.75% of revenue with no long-term supply contracts and receivable days at 93.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 4,000 TPA cutting capacity adds to take available capacity from 6,000 to 10,000 TPA, funded by ₹1,471.65 lakh IPO capex; machinery quotes dated 30 July 2026 with no orders placed yet, so timing is plan-based but not firmly committed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Actual production 5,257 TPA in FY26 at 87.62% utilisation is near capacity, and the 4,000 TPA expansion lifts available capacity to 10,000 TPA, so volume growth depends on the expansion coming live.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY26 utilisation at 87.62% on 15,000 TPA installed base (up from 78.20% in FY24), and the ₹1,537.31 lakh capex plan is already set out with machinery quotes, so further capex is likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Working capital sized for revenue targets of ₹2,756 lakh (FY27) and ₹3,359.94 lakh (FY28), with available capacity rising 67% from 6,000 to 10,000 TPA, but no explicit revenue growth % is given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Working capital gap grows from ₹1,916.67 lakh (FY26) to ₹3,359.94 lakh (FY28), and machinery quotes are valid only 180 days with no orders placed, so cost escalation on ₹1,537 lakh capex is a risk.

rows.label: Top 10 customer concentration and no long-term contracts
rows.why: Top 10 customers are 25.06% of FY26 revenue (FY24: 28.02%) with no long-term contracts, so demand visibility is limited.

rows.label: Sheela Foam trademark suit (claim ₹200.10 lakh)
rows.why: Mediation failed and the next hearing is 27 Nov 2026 on a ₹200.10 lakh claim, so an adverse outcome could hit the P&L.

rows.label: Payable days stretch and working capital gap
rows.why: Payable days rose to 84 in FY26 from 47 in FY24 and are projected to fall to 75 by FY28, while the working capital gap reaches ₹3,359.94 lakh, which pressures cash flow.

tone.note: This is a prospectus, not an earnings call, so there is no management Q&A; the document is confident about the Ambala expansion and capacity but heavily caveated on timelines, litigation and cost estimates.
